page: OVHcloud b2-7 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 2 vCPUs. Memory capacity is 7.0 GB, yielding 3.5 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 50 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the lower tiers of performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1072.92, while the multi-core score is 2156.87. Geekbench testing shows a single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1573.0, both falling into the bottom 10 percent of tested servers. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these limitations, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 944.93 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 17.27 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is measured at 178.89 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.07 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and bundled 50 GB SSD provide a predictable resource profile for low-demand workloads without the risk of CPU steal. However, the low benchmark-per-resource ratios indicate that this server is not suited for compute-intensive or high-throughput database applications. It is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose tasks such as static web serving, basic text processing, or small-scale development environments.
